_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 3 Computing unit lecture film, Lesson 10 Spreadsheets. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order: the grid, the formats, the filter, recording, and a range with its total. The Computing kit has no ART.sim - its spreadsheet is a closure inside its activity - so the grid is drawn in the engine's idiom, with the lesson's OWN data: the class pocket-money sheet, the bake-sale sheet and the six children of the filter table. Every number the voice says is computed in the pictures from those cells, never typed twice.
title: Spreadsheets
subtitle: Grade 3 Computing
objectives: Know that spreadsheets are comprised of rows and columns of cells and that data can be entered into the cells.
Know how to format cells according to their purpose, such as date, currency and text.
Demonstrate how to select data based upon their characteristics to solve problems.
Know how to record discrete and categorical data, using computing devices.

beats.say: A spreadsheet is a grid of cells. Columns go down and rows go across.
Column B, row 3 is cell B3. That is how every cell gets its name.
Here is the class pocket-money sheet. Names, ages and pocket money.
Each column has a letter across the top: A, B and C.
Each row has a number down the side. One, two, three, four.
A cell is named by its column letter and then its row number.
Column B, row 3 is cell B3. It holds Sami's age: seven.
Letter first, then number. B3 is a cell. 3B is not a cell.
The bake-sale sheet. A cell's format says what kind of thing it holds.
Column B holds dates. Format it as date and the sheet can sort them.
Column C holds money. Format it as currency to show pounds and pence.
Cell D4 holds the word Books, and a word is text.
Format everything as text and the sheet cannot sort dates or add money.

scenes.heading: Pick out the rows you need

beats.say: Six children, one row each, with their pet, their age and their club.
A filter selects the rows that share a characteristic, in a blink.
Who has a dog? Choose the field pet, choose dog, and press Filter.
Zara's row and Omar's row light up. Two children have a dog.
Now filter age, more than 7. Four rows match: Amal, Zara, Leo, Nora.
Typing a value into a cell is recording data on a computing device.
Zara gets four pounds. Tap cell C4 on the tablet and put a 4 in it.
Some data is a number you count. Some is a word that says which kind.

at.word: a word that says which kind

beats.say: Cell C4 holds a number. Cell A4 holds a word. Both are data.
Now the sheet can do the work. Format it, filter it, sort it, add it up.
That is why so much of the world's data lives in spreadsheets.
One cell has one name. A range is a block of cells from one to another.
You write it with a colon. C2 to C4 means every cell from C2 down to C4.
Select the range and format all three cells as currency in one go.
Ask for the total. Eighteen, twenty-five and thirty make seventy-three.
Change the thirty to forty and the total changes on its own: eighty-three.
A paper table cannot do that. The answer keeps itself right.
A cell has a column letter and a row number, and data goes in it.
Format each cell for its purpose, and filter to pick the rows you need.
Select a range, ask for the total, and the sheet keeps the answer right.
